value.conventions: money = float dollars; percentages = fractions; lookup miss = None; no tax logic in pricing.py

why: Source data stores price_cents (int) and discount_pct (int percent). Converting to team standard (float dollars, fraction) at load time so invoice.py and tax.py receive the same representation. Customer region is exposed so tax.py can look up the tax rule by region without pricing.py knowing tax rules.

value.region: customer region code string (e.g. TX), or None for an unknown customer
value.discount_pct: customer discount in percent numbers (10 means 10%), int or float
value.returns: total tax in integer cents, rounded half up
value.exempt: tax.py decides exemption from the category; caller does not filter
value.other: tax_pct_for_region(region) -> float, raises KeyError for an unknown region string

why: Team standard: integer cents, percent numbers, KeyError on missing lookup. Tax is computed only in tax.py; invoice.py passes pricing data in and uses the returned cents.

value: region=None (unknown customer) returns 0 tax with no error; any non-None region not in rates.csv raises KeyError
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, which conflicts with the KeyError convention. This reconciles them: an unknown customer is a None region, while an unknown region code is a lookup miss.

Units conflict with pricing_interface (open, v1). My team standard is float dollars and fractional percentages, and pricing.py's API is built on it. Proposal: one shared representation across all three modules, either (a) float dollars + fractions everywhere, with tax.py rounding to cents internally and returning float dollars, or (b) if the group prefers cents, I will return price_cents and discount_pct as integers from pricing.py. Please pick one; I will follow whatever is committed. Lookup misses: I return None; tax_pct_for_region raising KeyError is fine for tax.py's internal use.
invoice.py calls get_item(sku) and get_customer(id) as specified; converts float dollars/fractions to Decimal internally via Decimal(str(x)).

invoice.py passes known lines only as (amount_cents, category), region from get_customer (None for unknown customer), discount_pct = fraction*100, and uses the returned int cents. Display percent from tax_pct_for_region(region); 0% when region is None. KeyError for unknown region code propagates.
invoice.py passes region=None for unknown customers and shows 0% tax.
